subject: Likelihood family for zero-inflated positive-valued continuous data

messages.author: f2baaf6252beabe3
messages.subject: Likelihood family for zero-inflated positive-valued continuous data
parts:
Hi all, 

I'm working on a model where the outcome is mean duration of dengue outbreaks in districts in Peru over 2016-2018. Most districts experienced no outbreaks so the majority of rows are 0. Which likelihood family in INLA would you recommend?

Thanks,
Julianne

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Likelihood family for zero-inflated positive-valued continuous data
parts:
Hi Julianne,

If the 0s are true zeroes, I would recommend the Poisson. If they are possibly fake 0s, you can use some type of zero-inflation.

If there are different processes for zeroes and counts you can use hurdle model.

I think Alain Zuur (highland statistics) describes it quite well in his books.

Best,
Haakon

poisson/etc has two versions, buts are pretty basic in the zero-
model. its possible to use the trick (see the SPDE book online), which
have a separate model for the zeros and one for the non-zeros. the
book gives the details.

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Likelihood family for zero-inflated positive-valued continuous data
parts:
Hi all, 

I've sat down to work on the hurdle model this AM, and realized I neglected to highlight previously that I'm fitting a discrete (ICAR) model. I haven't been able to find any examples of a discrete hurdle model, and am running into issues with coding this. I'm trying the following:

dengue$z.intercept<-dengue$y.intercept<-rep(1, nrow(dengue))
dengue$s2<-dengue$si<-dengue$s
dengue$duration.y<-ifelse(dengue$duration==0, 0,1)#Binomial
dengue$duration.z<-ifelse(dengue$duration>0, dengue$duration, NA)#Gamma

formula <- c(duration.y, duration.z) ~ -1 + y.intercept + z.intercept+ SumSmean2 + f(s,model="besag", graph="ENSO.graph") + f(s2, copy="s") + f(s.i,model="iid")  
res <- inla(formula, family=c("binomial","gamma"), data=dengue, control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))

I get the error:

Error in inla(formula_summer, family = list("binomial", "gamma"), data = dengue_summer,  : 
  Number of families 2 does not match number of response variables 3702

When instead I do:

res <- inla(formula, family=c(rep("binomial", nrow(dengue)), rep("gamma", nrow(dengue)), data=dengue, control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))

I get the error:

Error in eval(predvars, data, env) : object 'y...fake' not found

I've also tried building a stack with A=1, but again I get the "Number of families error"

Any suggestions on how to code this?

Thanks,
Julianne

Everything is running smoothly, but I'm getting much larger coefficients than I had expected (my purpose is spatial regression). As a check I ran both a hurdle model (binomial and Poisson) and a zero-inflated Poisson on zero-inflated count data from the same dataset. The results are as follows:
